title: The Tale of the Envious and the Envied

paragraphs.en: In a city, two men lived in adjacent houses. One envied the other intensely, doing everything to harm him. Despite his efforts, the envied man prospered, while the envious one grew more miserable.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个城市里，有两户人家紧挨着。一个男人嫉妒他的邻居，千方百计想要陷害他。尽管他费尽心机，被嫉妒的人却越来越发达，而那个嫉妒的人则愈发痛苦。

paragraphs.en: Finally, the envied man left for another city and built a hermitage by an old well. He devoted himself to worship, and soon many mendicants sought him out.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，被嫉妒的人搬到了另一个城市，在一口古井旁建起了一座隐居小屋。他专心于修行，不久便吸引了许多乞丐前来求教。

paragraphs.en: The envious neighbor heard of this and visited the hermitage. The envied greeted him warmly but asked to speak privately. They walked to the edge of the well, where the envious pushed his friend into it, believing he had killed him.
paragraphs.zh: 嫉妒的邻居听说了这件事，便拜访了隐士住所。被嫉妒的人热情地迎接他，但请求私下交谈。他们走到井边，被嫉妒的人将朋友推入井中，以为他已经死了。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused, and Dinarzad remarked on the strange tale. Shahrazad hinted that tomorrow's story would be even more captivating.
paragraphs.zh: 沙里拉兹顿了顿，丁尔拉兹对这个奇怪的故事发表了看法。沙里拉兹暗示明天的故事将会更加引人入胜。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad asked her sister Shahrazad, "Tell us what happened to the envious after he pushed the envied into the well." Shahrazad replied, "Very well."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达问她的妹妹沙赫拉兹黛：“你刚才讲的那个嫉妒者把被嫉妒者推入井中后发生了什么事？”沙赫拉兹黛回答说，“好吧，我来讲给你听。”

paragraphs.en: The second dervish told the demon: "I heard that the envious threw the envied into an ancient well. Demons caught him and seated him on a rock, asking if they knew who he was. They didn't, but one said he was the envied who lived in our city, built this hermitage, and delighted us with his prayers and Quran recitations.
paragraphs.zh: 第二个修道士对恶魔说：“我听说那个嫉妒心强的人把被嫉妒者扔进了一个古井里。恶魔捉住了他，让他坐在一块岩石上，问他是否知道自己是谁。他们不知道，但其中一人说他是生活在我们城里的被嫉妒者，建了这座隐居处，并用他的祈祷和念诵《古兰经》使我们感到愉悦。”

paragraphs.en: The envious tricked him and threw him into the well. Tonight, the king plans to visit because his daughter is possessed by demon Maimun ibn-Damdam."
paragraphs.zh: 嫉妒者设下陷阱，将他推入了井中。今晚国王打算前来探望，因为他的女儿被名为梅穆恩·伊本-达马德的恶魔附身了。

paragraphs.en: The dervish said the cure was simple: pluck seven white hairs from a black cat's tail with a white spot at the end, burn them, and fumigate the girl.
paragraphs.zh: 苦行僧说，治疗方法很简单：从一只尾部有一小白点的黑猫身上拔下七根白毛，烧掉这些毛，然后给女孩进行熏蒸。

paragraphs.en: When dawn came, mendicants found the holy man climbing out of the well. He grew even more respected. The envied searched for the black cat, found it, and plucked seven hairs from its tail, keeping them.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明时分，乞丐们发现那位圣人正从井中爬出。他的声望因此更加崇高。那些心怀嫉妒的人四处寻找那只黑猫，终于找到了它，并拔下了七根毛，小心翼翼地收了起来。

paragraphs.en: The king arrived with his troops at dawn. He dismounted with the lords of the realm and instructed the rest to stay outside. Entering the hermitage, the envied welcomed him and asked if he wished to consult about his daughter's condition.
paragraphs.zh: 国王带着军队黎明时分抵达。他下马与诸位贵族一同进入，吩咐其他人留在外面。走进隐士的住所后，那位备受羡慕者迎接了国王，并询问他是否愿意咨询自己女儿的情况。

paragraphs.en: The king agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 国王同意了。

paragraphs.en: "Send for your daughter," the envied said. She was brought in, bound and fettered. He seated her behind a curtain, burned the hairs, and fumigated her with smoke.
paragraphs.zh: 被羡慕者吩咐道：“把你的女儿叫来。”女孩被带了进来，手脚都被绑着。他让她坐在帘子后面，烧掉了她的头发，并用烟雾对她进行了熏蒸。

paragraphs.en: At that moment, the demon inside her cried out and departed. She instantly recovered and asked what had happened. The king rejoiced, kissed his daughter's eyes, and thanked the envied.
paragraphs.zh: 就在这时，她内心的恶魔突然脱口而出，随即消失。她立刻恢复了常态，询问发生了什么事。国王喜出望外，亲吻了女儿的眼睑，并向那些被嫉妒的人表示感谢。

paragraphs.en: Turning to the lords, he asked who should marry the envied. They suggested his daughter. The king agreed, making the envied his son-in-law.
paragraphs.zh: 转向那些贵族，他问道谁来迎娶那位被嫉妒的对象。贵族们建议是他女儿。国王同意了这个提议，这样一来，被嫉妒的人就成了他的女婿。

paragraphs.en: Soon after, the vizier died, and the king appointed the envied as his successor. Later, the king also passed away, and the envied became the new monarch.
paragraphs.zh: 不久之后，首相去世，国王任命那位备受嫉妒的人为他的继任者。后来，国王也离世了，那位备受嫉妒的人继而登上了王位。

paragraphs.en: One day, as he rode with his entourage...
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，当他与随从们一同出行……

paragraphs.en: But Shahrazad paused, and Dinarzad remarked, "What a fascinating tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night to hear more if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 但是沙海拉扎德停下了，迪纳兹达remarked道：“真是个引人入胜的故事！”沙海拉扎德回答说：“如果国王饶恕我，明天晚上你就能听到更多。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad said, "Sister, continue the story of the envious and the envied." Shahrazad began: "I heard that the second dervish told the girl about his encounter with the demon..."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达说：“姐姐，请继续讲述那个嫉妒者与被嫉妒者的故事。”沙赫拉扎德开口道：“我听说第二个苦行僧向那女孩讲述了他与妖魔相遇的经历……”

paragraphs.en: One day, as the envied rode in his royal carriage at the head of his nobles, he noticed the envious. He instructed a vizier to bring the envious without alarming him. The vizier returned with the envious, who was then given one thousand weights of gold and twenty loads of goods before being escorted back to his town.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，那位备受羡慕的人乘坐华丽的皇家马车，在众贵族簇拥下出行时，注意到了那个心怀嫉妒之人。他吩咐一位大臣不要惊动对方，将那个心怀嫉妒之人带来见他。大臣回来后带来了那个人，随后那人被赐予了一千重金和二十车货物，然后又被护送回了他的城镇。

paragraphs.en: I spoke to the demon, "O demon, consider how mercifully the envied treated the envious, despite their long-standing animosity." I wept and recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 我对恶魔说：“哦，恶魔，请想想被嫉妒的人尽管与嫉妒者有着长久的敌意，仍以多么仁慈的态度对待他们。”我边说边流泪，并吟诵着这些诗句：

paragraphs.en: Pardon my crime, for every mighty judge Is used to mercy some offenders show. I stand before you guilty of all sins, But you the ways of grace and mercy know.
paragraphs.zh: 原谅我的罪过，因为每一位公正的法官都会对一些犯错者施以宽恕。我站在这里，承认自己罪无可逭，但你们懂得恩典与宽容之道。

paragraphs.en: For he who seeks forgiveness from above, Should pardon the offenders here below.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，向上帝求得宽恕的人，应当在此世间原谅那些犯错者。

paragraphs.en: The demon replied, "I will not kill you, but I will put you under a spell." He then transformed me into an ape by sprinkling dust on me.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔回答说：“我不会杀你，但我会施一个咒。”随后，他向我洒了些许尘土，将我变成了一只猿猴。

paragraphs.en: Upon discovering that I was an ape, I wept for myself and blamed life. Descending the mountain, I wandered through a vast desert for a month before reaching the seashore. Standing by the shore, I saw a ship sailing towards me under favorable winds.
paragraphs.zh: 得知自己是一只猿猴后，我为自己哭泣，并抱怨命运的不公。下山后，我在一片广阔的沙漠中游荡了一个月，才终于抵达海边。站在海边，我看到一艘船在顺风中向我驶来。

paragraphs.en: Using a branch from a tree, I signaled desperately but could not cry out. The ship turned toward the shore, revealing it to be a large vessel filled with merchants and goods.
paragraphs.zh: 我用一根树枝拼命地挥舞着求救，却无法大声呼喊。船只转向岸边，露出那是一艘大型商船，满载着商人和货物。

paragraphs.en: When they spotted me, the merchants accused me of bringing bad luck and suggested killing or shooting me. In despair, I clung to the captain's gown, tears streaming down my face. The captain and some merchants were taken aback by my plea for protection.
paragraphs.zh: 一见到我，商人们指控我是不祥之人，建议要么杀死我，要么射杀我。绝望中，我紧紧抓住船长的外衣，泪水如雨般流下。船长和一些商人对我求保护的话感到惊讶。

paragraphs.en: The captain declared that he would care for me, warning his men not to harm me. He treated me kindly, though I could only nod in understanding.
paragraphs.zh: 船长宣布他会照顾我，并警告手下不要伤害我。尽管他只能点点头表示理解，他对我的态度还算不错。

paragraphs.en: Thus, I learned to follow his commands silently, despite my inability to speak.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，尽管我无法开口说话，我还是学会了默默地遵从他的命令。

paragraphs.en: After a fifty-day voyage under favorable winds, we arrived at a bustling city. Upon anchoring, messengers from the king approached us with a scroll for each of us to write one line. The vizier had passed away, and the king vowed to appoint only someone as skilled in calligraphy.
paragraphs.zh: 经过五十天的顺风航行，我们抵达了一个繁华的城市。停泊后，国王派来的使者每人递给我们一张卷轴，让我们各自写下一行字。原来，首相去世了，国王发誓要任命一位书法同样出色的接任者。

paragraphs.en: I seized the scroll, much to their alarm, fearing I might damage it. However, I assured them that I would write on it. They were astonished, having never seen an ape write before.
paragraphs.zh: 我一把抓过卷轴，把他们吓了一跳，生怕我会弄坏它。不过，我向他们保证自己会在上面写字。他们大感惊讶，因为从没见过猿猴会写字。

paragraphs.en: The captain said he would discipline me if my writing was poor but promised to adopt me if it was good, praising my intelligence and manners.
paragraphs.zh: 船长说如果我的文章写得不好就会严厉管教我，但如果写得好则会收留我，并称赞了我的聪明和礼貌。

paragraphs.en: With the pen dipped in ink, I wrote in Ruqa’ script: Time’s record of the favors of the great Has been effaced by your greater favor. Of you your children God will not deprive, You, being to grace both mother and father.
paragraphs.zh: 蘸着墨水的笔，我用鲁卡伊字体书写：时光记载的伟大恩赐 已被你更大的恩典抹去。你的孩子们不会因你而失去天恩，你是恩宠的母亲与父亲。

paragraphs.en: Next, in Muhaqqiq script: His pen has showered bounty everywhere And without favor favored every land. Yet even the Nile, which destroys the earth, Cannot its ink use with such mighty hand.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，用穆哈qqiq体书写：他的笔洒下了无尽的恩惠 每一片土地都得到了眷顾。就连尼罗河，那毁灭大地的河流 也无法如此豪迈地挥洒它的墨水。

paragraphs.en: Then in Raihani script: I swore, whoever uses me to write, By the One, Peerless, Everlasting God, That he would never any man deny With one of the pen’s strokes his livelihood.
paragraphs.zh: 然后用raihani体书写：我发誓，无论谁使用我来写作，凭那位独一无二、永恒不朽的真主之名，他绝不会因为我的一支笔而剥夺任何人的生计。

paragraphs.en: Finally, in Naskhi script: There is no writer who from death will flee, But what his hand has written time will keep. Commit to paper nothing then, except What you would like on Judgment Day to see.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，用纳希体字体书写：没有作家会逃避死亡，但时间会保存他所写下的文字。因此，在纸上只写下那些你希望在审判日看到的内容吧。

paragraphs.en: The second dervish spoke to the girl: "Take this scroll to the king," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 第二位苦行僧对女孩说：“把这个卷轴带给国王。”

paragraphs.en: When the messengers returned with the scroll, the king admired Shahrazad's writing. He rewarded her with a robe and a she-mule, instructing them to bring the writer to court as well.
paragraphs.zh: 当使者带着卷轴返回时，国王赞赏沙赫拉兹_ad的书法。他赏赐给她一件长袍和一匹母驴，并吩咐他们也要把这位作家带到宫廷来。

paragraphs.en: Dinarzad urged Shahrazad to continue the story: "Sister, tell us what happened next."
paragraphs.zh: 迪纳兹德催促莎赫拉兹德继续讲故事：“姐姐，接着说吧，接下来发生了什么？”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad recounted how the messengers returned with the king’s command. They dressed her in the robe and placed her on the she-mule, causing a commotion in the city. People gathered to see the spectacle.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉扎德讲述了信使们带着国王的命令返回的故事。他们给她穿上礼服，让她骑上母驴，顿时城中闹哄哄的。人们纷纷聚集起来，想一睹这番景象。

paragraphs.en: As they approached the palace, the king's messengers arrived again. They led Shahrazad to the king, who was eager to meet the writer of such fine script. The whole city buzzed with excitement, whispering that the king had appointed an ape as vizier.
paragraphs.zh: 他们刚接近王宫，国王的使者又到了。他们将沙赫拉兹带到国王面前，国王急切地想要见一见这位书写如此优美文字的人。整个城市都充满了兴奋的低语，传说国王竟然任命了一只猿猴为首相。

paragraphs.en: Upon entering the king's presence, I prostrated and bowed three times before kissing the ground. The king himself marveled at my manners, granting permission for his retinue to leave. Only a servant, a Mamluk, and myself remained.
paragraphs.zh: 我躬身三次，拜倒在地上吻地。国王对我如此得体的举止赞叹不已，允许他的随从先行退出。只剩下一名仆人、一名马木鲁克和我自己。

paragraphs.en: The king ordered a table set with food and invited me to eat. After washing my hands seven times, I sat on my knees and ate modestly as befitting the occasion. Then, taking pen and inkwell, I wrote:
paragraphs.zh: 国王吩咐摆上宴席，请我共进晚餐。我洗净双手七次，跪坐着谦逊地用餐，以符合场合的礼仪。随后，我拿起笔和墨水写道：

paragraphs.en: Wail for the crane well-stewed in tangy sauce; Mourn for the meat, either well baked or fried; Cry for the hens and daughters of the grouse And the fried birds, even as I have cried.
paragraphs.zh: 为那酸辣炖鹤哀叹， 为烤肉或油炸肉惋惜； 为鹌鹑及其女儿哭泣， 也为油炸鸟儿，正如我所泣诉。

paragraphs.en: Two kinds of fish on plain bread, sizzling eggs, While grilled meat with pickled greens is my delight. In porridge at night, hunger gnaws under light. O soul, be patient; fate's fickle hand takes flight.
paragraphs.zh: 两条鱼夹在普通面包中，煎蛋吱吱作响，烤肉配腌菜更是我的最爱。夜幕下的粥里，饥饿在灯光下悄然噬咬。哦，灵魂，请耐心些；命运多变的手已翩然远去。

paragraphs.en: The king read the verses and pondered. Wine was then served in a glass flagon. The king drank first, offering me some.
paragraphs.zh: 国王读完这些诗句后沉思了一会儿。随后，酒被倒入一个玻璃壶中。国王先喝了酒，然后递给我一些。

paragraphs.en: I kissed his ground before taking a sip and wrote:
paragraphs.zh: 我亲吻了地面才敢小口品尝，并写道：

paragraphs.en: For my confession they burned me with fire And found that I was for endurance made. Hence I was borne high on men's hands, And given to kiss the lips of pretty maid.
paragraphs.zh: 为了我的忏悔，他们用火烤炙 我因此被认定为坚忍不屈之人。 因此我被人高举双手， 并被赐予亲吻那些貌美的少女的嘴唇。

paragraphs.en: The king praised my chess skills after our games. He declared, "If a man had such cultivation, he would excel all others." We played three matches; I won the second and third.
paragraphs.zh: 国王在对弈之后称赞了我的棋艺，说道：“若有人有这样的修养，定能胜过众人。”我们共进行了三局对弈，我赢得了第二局和第三局。

paragraphs.en: Impressed, he asked me to write about it.
paragraphs.zh: impressed，他让我把这件事写下来。

paragraphs.en: I wrote: Two armies all day long with arms contend, Bringing the battle always to a head. But when night’s cover on them does descend The two go sleeping in a single bed.
paragraphs.zh: 我写道：“整日里两军刀光剑影，战斗一触即发。夜幕降临，双方却同榻而眠。”

paragraphs.en: The king admired my verse. He instructed his servant Muqbil, "Go to your lady Sitt al-Husn and tell her that her father summons her to see this strange ape and enjoy the spectacle."
paragraphs.zh: 国王赞赏我的诗篇。他吩咐仆人穆克比勒：“去你那位名叫斯蒂特·阿·胡森的夫人那里，告诉她她的父亲要她前来一见这只奇怪的猴子，并一同欣赏这场奇观。”

paragraphs.en: The eunuch returned with the king's daughter. She veiled her face and accused me, saying, "Father, have you lost your honor by exposing me to men?" Astonished, the king asked, "Daughter, there is no one here but this Mamluk, your mentor, and I, your father."
paragraphs.zh: 太监带着国王的女儿回来了。她遮住了脸，指责我说：“父亲，你把我暴露给男人，难道就丢掉了你的尊严吗？”国王惊讶地问道：“女儿，除了这位马穆鲁克——你的导师以及我，你的父亲之外，这里根本没有其他人。”

paragraphs.en: She replied, "From this young man enchanted by a demon's son who turned him into an ape after killing his wife. You think he’s wise, but he’s foolish."
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说：“这位被妖孽之子迷惑的年轻人，杀妻变猿，如今只落得这般境地。你以为他聪明，其实愚不可及。”

paragraphs.en: The king was amazed and asked me if it was true. I nodded yes. He then turned to his daughter, asking how she knew of the enchantment.
paragraphs.zh: 国王惊讶不已，问我这是否属实。我点了点头表示肯定。接着他转向女儿，询问她是如何得知这个魔法的。

paragraphs.en: She replied that from childhood, a witch taught her magic, allowing her to transport stones beyond Mount Qaf in an hour.
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说，从小就有个巫婆教她魔法，让她能在一小时内把石头运过卡夫山。

paragraphs.en: The king declared, "Deliver him from the spell; make him vizier and marry you." She agreed with pleasure. But morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent.
paragraphs.zh: 国王宣布：“解除他的魔咒，让他做你的宰相，然后你嫁给他。”她欣然应允。然而天亮时分，沙哈拉兹达却沉默不语了。

paragraphs.en: Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait for tomorrow's tale if I live."
paragraphs.zh: 迪纳兹达说：“姐姐，这真是个奇怪的故事！”沙赫拉扎德回答道：“如果我还活着，你就要等到明天的故事了。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister to tell another tale: "If you're not sleepy, tell us one of your stories."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳扎德催促她的妹妹讲一个故事：“如果你不困，给我们讲一个你的故事吧。”

paragraphs.en: The king’s daughter drew a circle in the palace hall with a knife engraved in Hebrew, inscribing Kufic letters and talismanic words. She muttered charms, and darkness fell. Suddenly, a lion-like demon appeared, and she cried out, "Get away, you dog!"
paragraphs.zh: 王女在宫殿的大厅里用一把刻有希伯来文的刀划了一个圆圈，里面写满了库法体字母和符咒文字。她低声念着咒语，黑暗骤然降临。突然间，一只像狮子般的恶魔出现了，她惊叫道：“滚开，你这畜生！”

paragraphs.en: The demon challenged her, saying they had sworn not to cross paths. She retorted, "Cursed one, how could I keep a pledge with such a creature?" The demon lunged, but she plucked a hair from her head, waved it, and transformed it into a sword.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔向她挑战，说他们曾发誓不相遇。她反驳道：“该死的东西，我怎么可能对这样的生物守信？”说着，恶魔扑了过来，但她随手拔下一根头发，挥了挥，这根头发竟化作了一把利剑。

paragraphs.en: She struck the lion in half, but its head turned into a scorpion. The girl then morphed into a serpent and fought the scorpion for a long time before turning into an eagle to chase it away.
paragraphs.zh: 她一击将狮子劈为两半，但狮子的头却化作了蝎子。女孩随后变成了一条蛇，与蝎子激战了许久，最终化作一只鹰将其驱散。

paragraphs.en: The scorpion fled outside, transforming into a vulture. The girl followed as an eagle. After a while, the ground split, revealing a piebald cat that meowed and snored.
paragraphs.zh: 蝎子化作秃鹰逃了出去，女孩则变成了一只雄鹰紧随其后。不久，地面裂开，露出一只花斑猫，它喵喵叫着打起了呼噜。

paragraphs.en: A black wolf appeared, and they fought in the palace for a long time. Seeing defeat, the cat turned into a worm and hid inside a pomegranate by the fountain. The pomegranate grew large, and the wolf transformed into a white rooster.
paragraphs.zh: 一只黑狼出现了，它们在宫殿里激战了很长时间。眼看不敌，猫化作一条虫子，藏在一株水边的石榴树里。石榴越长越大，而狼则变成了白鸡。

paragraphs.en: The rooster picked up all the seeds except one hidden near the fountain. He cried and crowed, flapping his wings as if asking for more. Suddenly, he saw the remaining seed and rushed to pick it.
paragraphs.zh: 公鸡捡起了所有的种子，唯独有一颗被藏在喷泉附近。他一边叫着，一边扑腾翅膀，仿佛在乞求更多的种子。突然，他看到了那最后一颗种子，急忙跑过去啄了起来。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister Shahrazad to continue the story. "Sister, if you are not sleepy, tell us more," she said. Shahrazad replied, "With pleasure."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达催促她的妹妹沙赫拉兹达继续讲故事。“姐姐，如果你不困的话，给我们讲得再详细些吧。”她说。沙赫拉兹达回答道：“我很乐意。”

paragraphs.en: I heard, O King, that the second dervish told the girl a tale: The rooster, seeing the seed, rushed to pick it but rolled into a fountain and turned into a fish. It dove in, and the rooster followed, both disappearing for a long time. Loud shouts and howls echoed, and soon a demon emerged as a burning flame, followed by the girl also aflame.
paragraphs.zh: 我听，国王陛下说，第二个苦行僧给那女孩讲了一个故事：公鸡看见了谷粒，急忙去啄食，却不慎滚入了一眼泉中，化作了一条鱼。它潜入水中，公鸡紧随其后，两人一时间都消失不见了。喧哗和尖叫声此起彼伏，很快，一团火焰化作了恶魔现身，随后那女孩也燃起了熊熊烈火。

paragraphs.en: The demon battled the girl, their flames engulfing them. Smoke filled the palace, and we feared suffocation.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔与女孩激战，火焰将她们双双包围。烟雾弥漫整个宫殿，我们都担心窒息。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, the demon darted out of the fire, standing before us in the hall, blowing fire at us. The girl pursued him with a loud cry. A spark hit me, an ape-like figure, destroying my right eye.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，那个恶魔从火焰中窜出，站在大厅里对着我们喷火。女孩一声尖叫追了上去。一颗火星击中了我这个类猿的形象，摧毁了我的右眼。

paragraphs.en: Another burned half the king's face, including his beard and chin, knocking out several teeth. A third killed a servant instantly.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个人的灼伤则几乎烧毁了国王的脸部，包括他的胡须和下巴，还敲掉了几颗牙齿。第三个则当场杀死了一名仆人。

paragraphs.en: Just as we feared destruction, we heard, "God is great! He has conquered!" It was the king’s daughter who defeated the demon.
paragraphs.zh: 正当我们担心遭到毁灭的时候，突然听到有人喊：“上帝伟大！他战胜了恶魔！”原来国王的女儿击败了妖魔。

paragraphs.en: We saw only ashes where they had stood.
paragraphs.zh: 他们原先站立的地方只剩下灰烬。

paragraphs.en: The girl approached and asked for a bowl of water. She cried out, "In the name of God, be yourself again," sprinkling me with it. I transformed into a man.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩走过来要了一碗水，她喊道：“以神之名，做回你自己吧，”说着将水洒在我身上。我顿时化作一个男人。

paragraphs.en: She then shouted, "The fire! The fire!" She explained that she had been wounded by a demon's arrow and was dying.
paragraphs.zh: 她then喊道：“着火了！着火了！”她解释说，自己被妖魔的箭射中，伤势严重，恐怕活不了多久。

paragraphs.en: Despite her inexperience, she fought the demon successfully until he initiated a magic domain. She countered his domains with greater ones until she opened the fire domain. Few survive this, but with cunning and God’s help, she defeated him.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管她经验不足，但她成功地与恶魔对抗，直到对方发动了魔法领域。她以更强大的领域进行了反击，最终开启了火域。这种情况很少有人能存活下来，但凭借机智和上帝的帮助，她最终战胜了对方。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what an entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait till tomorrow night if I live."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德沉默不语。丁纳扎德说：“姐姐，真是个有趣的故事！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答道：“如果我还活着，你明天晚上再听吧。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad asked her sister, "If you're not sleepy, tell us one of your tales." Shahrazad agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达对她的妹妹说：“如果你不困，给我们讲一个你的故事吧。”沙赫拉扎德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O King, that the second dervish spoke to the girl.
paragraphs.zh: 我听闻，国王陛下，第二位苦行僧与那女孩交谈了。

paragraphs.en: The king's daughter cried out "The fire! The fire!" as sparks burned her legs, thighs, and bosom.
paragraphs.zh: 王女痛呼：“着火了！着火了！”火花灼烧得她腿、大腿乃至胸部疼痛难忍。

paragraphs.en: She kept shouting until she was reduced to ashes. Her father wept bitterly, causing the narrator to feel immense sorrow. When the king saw his daughter dead, he beat his face in grief, prompting the narrator to do the same.
paragraphs.zh: 她喊叫着直到声嘶力竭，最终化为灰烬。她的父亲悲痛欲绝地哭泣，让叙述者也感到无比哀伤。国王见女儿已死，捶胸顿足，Narrator 也随之痛哭流涕。

paragraphs.en: Statesmen and servants entered, shocked by the sight of two heaps of ashes and the king's distress.
paragraphs.zh: 朝臣和侍从们惊见两堆灰烬和国王愁容满面，纷纷步入殿中。

paragraphs.en: The king mourned for seven days before ordering a vaulted tomb built over his daughter’s remains but scattering the demon’s ashes. He then fell ill for a month until he recovered. Upon regaining health, he summoned the narrator and warned, "Young man, listen to me.
paragraphs.zh: 国王为女儿哀悼了七天，随后下令建造一座拱顶墓穴安葬她的遗体，而将恶魔的灰烬撒去。之后他病了一个月才康复。恢复健康后，国王召来叙述者，警告道：“年轻人，听我说。”

paragraphs.en: If you disobey, you will perish." The narrator assured him of obedience.
paragraphs.zh: “如果你不服从，就会身败名裂。”叙述者保证他会服从。

paragraphs.en: The king blamed the narrator for their misfortunes, saying his daughter's death, servant’s demise, and near destruction were all due to the narrator's presence. He declared, "We would have been happy if not for you. Now leave our city or face my wrath."
paragraphs.zh: 国王将所有的不幸都归咎于叙述者，说女儿的去世、仆人的死亡以及险些城池被毁都是因为他的到来。国王怒气冲冲地说道：“要不是因为你，我们会过得很好。现在要么离开我们的城市，要么承受我的雷霆之怒。”

paragraphs.en: The narrator left, dumbfounded by the king's anger.
paragraphs.zh: 叙述者被国王的怒气惊呆了，只好离开了。

paragraphs.en: Before leaving the city, I shaved my beard and eyebrows, donned a black woolen robe, and departed in sorrow. My grief over losing an eye and the deaths of two girls deepened as I recalled entering the capital. I wept and recited verses about enduring until God's will is fulfilled.
paragraphs.zh: 离开城市前，我刮了胡子和眉毛，穿上一件黑色羊毛衫，带着深深的哀伤启程。想起失去一只眼睛以及两位少女的离世，我的悲伤更加沉重。我边走边流泪，口中念诵着坚持到上帝意愿实现的诗句。

paragraphs.en: I traveled through many regions with the hope of reaching Baghdad to seek help from someone who could guide me to the Commander of the Faithful. That night, I arrived at this house, where a stranger greeted me. We walked together until we reached here.
paragraphs.zh: 我游历了多个地区，希望能到达巴格达，寻求一位能指引我去见哈里发的人的帮助。当晚，我抵达了这家房子，一个陌生人迎面而来。我们并肩走着，直到来到这里。

paragraphs.en: The girl told me to stroke my head and leave, but I insisted on hearing more tales before going. The black men untied me, and I stood beside one dervish.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩让我摸了摸头然后离开，但我坚持要听完更多的故事再走。黑人们解开了我的绳索，我站在了一个苦行僧身旁。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Her sister remarked that the story was strange yet entertaining. Shahrazad replied that it paled in comparison to what she would tell the next night if she survived.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。她的姐姐remarked那故事虽有些奇异却颇为引人入胜。沙赫拉兹阿德回应说，与她次日若能存活下来所要讲述的故事相比，这故事简直逊色不少。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad requested a tale from her sister. The king added his request for the dervishes' unfinished story. Shahrazad agreed and began her narrative.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹达向她妹妹请求一个故事。国王也加入了请求，希望听闻那些苦行僧未说完的故事。沙赫拉扎德应允了，并开始了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: The third dervish spoke to the king:
paragraphs.zh: 第三位圣士对国王说道：

paragraphs.en: All the scripts mentioned are variations of the cursive, flowing Arabic script. Early Qurans featured a different, more straight-lined script.
paragraphs.zh: 所有提到的字体都是草书体阿拉伯文的不同变体。早期的《古兰经》则使用一种更为直线排列的字体。
